findings.text: The help page names every command and every option, so adding the command `update` changes what cli.help.page must write. It is not among the candidates, even though the amendment changed the cli Rationale to say every command fits on one page.

install.update.missing's Then always writes the stdout line naming <file> as written, while install.update.exit says no stdout line names a file that failed to be written. For example, a missing skill below a `.claude` that is a file gets both. install.update.stamp avoids this with "where it could write it"; install.update.missing has no such qualifier.

[version stamp] is defined as the Proviso version of the `init` that wrote the file, but `update` now writes the files and stamps them with its own version (install.update.release). Today that is covered only by the wording "as `init` of its own Proviso version writes it".
The Rationale of install.version says refreshing what version reports is the job of `update`, but version also reports the spec tree model version, which update does not refresh yet.

install.update.keeps says every entry other than the skills and agent definitions stays byte for byte as it was, but a folder that gains a written skill is an entry that changes; install.init.keeps says every file.
